text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Many teams create feature branches for each new task, such as fixing a bug or adding a feature. This keeps the main branch safe and stable. When the work is finished, you merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes and give feedback. This workflow helps people work together, avoid mistakes, and keep a clear history of the project. Learning branches makes teamwork much easier.
